analysis:
The changes are test-only.

CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift:
- The header comments (head 10-12, 21) now say the suite runs in the provider CI lane instead of being skipped. This is a documentation change, not a control change.
- New tests 3c and 3d (head 456-491) verify reconnect behavior. A coordinator close with code 1012 should reconnect within 0-1s without backoff growth. A session that stays open past stableSessionDuration should reset the backoff.
- makeClient gains a reconnectPolicy parameter (head 652-653, 674-675).
- New helpers reregistrationTime and withGrownReconnectBackoff were added (head 679-727).

CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift is a new file covering the policy rows. Only patch excerpt lines 1-95 are visible; the file unit has metadata only.

Security relevance:
- The production CoordinatorReconnectPolicy/CoordinatorClient runLoop source is not in this batch.
- Integration should check how the policy behaves on TB-002 against adversarial or network-injected closes. The coordinator is trusted, but on-path close frames are only possible if TLS is absent.
- A 1012 fast-reconnect path could enable reconnect storms or availability issues if close codes are honored without bounds. The tests imply 1012 yields a 0-1s wait without growth. Because each wait stays at least about 0s, repeated 1012 closes could cause tight reconnect loops against the coordinator. That is coordinator-originated, though, and so trusted.
- Reconnect also interacts with T-053/TB-011: endpoint resumption, grant invalidation on connection change, and re-registration. Integration should confirm the production change does not carry authorization state across reconnects.

No regression is evident from the test code. The tests use mock keys and fake signatures only within the test scope.
